name: Secomber
summary: Small walled town on three stone hills on the north bank of the River Delimbiyr, where the Unicorn Run joins it; a stop on the Delimbiyr Route (Daggerford to the west, Zelbross and Loudwater to the east) with the Secomber Trail running north to Uluvin; farming, fishing, stone-cutting and caravan trade; hobgoblin tribute by 1479 DR.

identity.subregion: North bank of the River Delimbiyr at the mouth of the Unicorn Run; High Moor to the south
identity.ruler_office: Lord (14th century DR); no ruler recorded for the late 15th century

periods.lore_2e_3e: 1358 to 1372 DR (The Savage Frontier, Volo's Guide to the Sword Coast, The North, Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting)
periods.note: Nothing is verified for 1492 DR itself.

position.note: Taken from maps/locations.json; not a canonical georeference. The engine position is about 161 miles from Daggerford (SE14).

engine_record.population_note: Unchanged 1,300 is an undated engine estimate for the 1492 DR planning scenario, not a census or measured decline. The population report keeps 900 (1358 and 1367 DR), the 200-village/700-hamlet split (The North), and 1,417 (1372 DR) as historical evidence (SE4).
engine_record.business_note: Added 2026-10-15. The inns come from Volo's Guide to the Sword Coast (1994, set 1367 DR) and The North (1996); the two workshops from the Forgotten Realms Wiki (Forging the Realms, 2013, undated). Operation in 1492 DR is not verified for any; staff beyond the four Windfeather brothers is assumed.

area_geography.summary: Town on three stone hills north of the Delimbiyr; the Unicorn Run flows south along the east side to join the river; the Delimbiyr Route runs along the north bank from Daggerford (west) over the Unicorn Run to Zelbross and Loudwater (east); the Secomber Trail leaves the Route north to Uluvin; the High Moor lies south of the river.
routes: Delimbiyr Route (west to Daggerford and the Trade Way; east to Zelbross and Loudwater)
area_geography.orientation: North up, as drawn by the compass on the reference town maps; not confirmed by a written source.
sources: The North: Guide to the Savage Frontier (1996), pp. 63, 76 and Map of Interior
Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting (3rd edition), p. 228

town_plan.source: Three-hill town map of Secomber (wiki file Secomber.jpg, 4th-edition era, caption 1479 DR; publication not identified), stored in this folder as three copies of different resolution and colour
town_plan.stored_note: Reference images were added to reference_maps/ on 2026-10-15; provenance of the three-hill plan is not verified. caa1e... is the parchment version, 9966... a green-wash version and OIP(1).webp a small copy; all show the same plan.
town_plan.orientation: Compass rose at the west side, north up
layout: Three ring-shaped hills, each with houses on concentric rings, enclosed together by a wall that runs from the south side of the town round the north and east sides
A palisaded fort stands on the south-west hill
A pool and a cluster of larger buildings (inns and halls) lie in the middle, where the three hills meet
A road runs from the centre south-east to the junction on the Delimbiyr Route; a second road runs south-west to the Route
The Delimbiyr Route runs east to west along the river; the Secomber Trail leaves it at the junction and runs north to Uluvin
A wooden bridge carries the Route over the Unicorn Run to the east, towards Loudwater
A strip of buildings and about nine piers line the north bank of the Delimbiyr, with a few more buildings at the junction
A planted field lies in the north-west corner

other_reference_images.kind: Hand-drawn grid-paper map of a much larger, sprawling town with named lanes, numbered lots, a harbour and bridges over the Delimbiyr; marked as not to scale
other_reference_images.source: Probably the NineLizards fan project (Secomber II, a campaign text its author dates to about 1992); attributed by matching labels, not by a published credit
other_reference_images.note: Layout differs from the three-stone-hills plan; its lane, lot and district names (Skipper's Ave, Rumble Market, The Dip, Winterstay, Goodhill, Lord's Hill, Harbour Hill, the Flanks) are not confirmed canon and were not used.

other_reference_images.kind: Digital map with nine numbered sites, a wide Delimbiyr and bridges to the south bank; no legend
other_reference_images.note: Layout differs from the three-hill plan; not used.

uncertain_readings: The three-hill plan is 4th-edition era and unscaled, so no distances can be taken from it
The named buildings (Tower of Amelior Amanitas, Singing Sprite, Seven-Stringed Harp) cannot be placed on it

wall_status_by_period.14th century DR: palisaded fort on one hill; no town wall recorded
wall_status_by_period.1479 DR: town wall recorded (Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide, p. 37; shown on the three-hill plan)
wall_status_by_period.1492 DR: unresolved; a later claim that the walls were removed has not been read in its source

sketch.method: Single panel drawn by eye from the three-hill town plan and the written sources. Three hills drawn as contour rings with a ring of house markers on each; palisaded fort on the south-west hill; wall circuit, road spine, pool and number of piers assumed; River Delimbiyr along the south, Unicorn Run along the east with a wooden bridge on the Delimbiyr Route; Secomber Trail north.
sketch.status: Working reconstruction, not a copy of a published map
assumed: Road spine from the centre to the Route
Number and positions of harbour piers
Size and position of the pool in the centre

climate.label: Cool, cloudy, subarctic inland North
climate.band: subarctic (Spine of the World to Waterdeep), by inference; the source does not place Secomber

summer.notes: short, humid, warm breezes; rain usual with hail, sleet and snow common; near-unbroken cloud; wizard weather near the High Forest

winter.notes: heavy snow in the midlands, frequent blizzards with drifts often 10 feet deep, rivers frozen between Uktar and early Ches thick enough for wagons

not_described: Table 1 monthly temperatures (illegible in the scan)
local_sourced: Singing Sprite cold and damp in winter, warmer and damp in summer (Volo's Guide to the Sword Coast, p. 83)
Unicorn Run a cool, clear river from the High Forest (Volo's Guide to the Sword Coast, p. 79)
inference: Inland and level with Waterdeep on the engine map (y 1194.4 against 1200), so the subarctic description is the closest fit
A frozen Delimbiyr would likely halt or reroute river traffic from Daggerford
climate.model_class_note: The model class for Secomber is temperate (SE16).
